AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to enacting the "New York

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S10344

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to enacting the "New York
travel insurance act" regulating the licensing and registration of trav-
el insurance agents and travel retailers, and the sale and marketing of
travel insurance and related products

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to regulate the licensing and registration
of Limited lines travel insurance producers and travel retailers, in
addition to the sale and marketing of travel insurance and related
products.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Establishes this bill as the "New York insurance act."

Section 2: Amends section 3435 of insurance law by adding subsection
(e).

Section 3: Amends section 3452 of the insurance law is amended by adding
subsection (e).

Section 4: Amends subsection (i) of section 2101 of insurance taw, which
includes the sale of travel-related products and services in the defi-
nition of "limited licensee."

Section 5: Amends section 2131 of the insurance law pertaining to limit-
ed licenses for rental vehicle companies, peer-to-peer car sharing
program administrators, wireless communications equipment vendors and
self-service storage companies to also pertain to travel insurance
agents and the sale or soliciting of travel-related products and
services.

Subsection 4 outlines applicable coverages that can be issued as an
individual policy to the consumer, as a group, or blanket policy.
Subparagraph (E) establishes that providers must cover the price, deduc-
tible, benefits, exclusions or other limitations of policies; travel
agents specifically must provide a description of the material terms or
actual material terms of the insurance coverage.

Subparagraph (F) provides that with respect to travel insurance, travel
retailers are permitted to provide general information about the insur-
ance offered by the travel retailer but is not qualified or authorized
to answer technical questions about terms and conditions of the insur-
ances the retailer offers, nor can the retailer evaluate the adequacy of
the customer's existing coverage.

Subparagraph (G) establishes that customers may cancel insurance at any
time and any unearned premiums will be refunded in accordance with
applicable law. With respect to travel insurance, the provider has to
offer a description of the review of cancellation process for the travel
insurance policy Subsection 3 subparagraph (f) provides for rates to be
subject to article 23 of this chapter. Brochures and other written mate-
rials provided by travel agents shall be subject to section 2131
subsection (1) of this chapter. Subdivision (2) notes that each travel
insurance agency shalt require each employee and authorized represen-
tative of each registered retailer, whose duties include offering and
disseminating travel insurance, to receive a program of instruction or
training subject to the discretion of the superintended for review and
approval. Provides minimum requirements for training.

Subdivision (1) with respect to travel insurance outlines the conditions
for which a travel retailer may offer and disseminate travel insurance
on behalf of and under the license of a travel insurance agent. Includes
definitions for this section.

Section 6: Establishes article 81 to insurance law, "Travel Insurance."

8101: Establishes legislative scope and intent of the article.

8102: Defines terms for article 81.

8103: Establishes the conditions for offering travel plans as one price
for combined features in New York.

8104: Outlines the framework for sales practices of travel insurance.

8105: Provides conditions for travel administrators.

8106: Establishes that travel insurance shall be classified and filed
for purposes of rates and forms under an inland marine line of insur-
ance.

8107: Establishes that the superintendent may promogulated regulations
to implement provisions of this article.

Section 7 establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill seeks to establish a consistent regulatory framework for the
travel insurance industry in New York State. This act would create
uniform definitions, expand and codify the ability to write travel
insurance as a blanket or group product, clarify the payment of premium
taxes, setting out permitted and prohibited sales practices, and gener-
ally reducing regulatory confusion.

Insurance regulation in the United States is managed on a state-by-state
basis. If an insurer wants to sell products to customers in more than
one state, they may encounter additional bureaucracy and expenses to
ensure compliance in all of them. The New York Travel Insurance Act
seeks to put New York's travel insurance regulations in line with 40
other states that have already adopted a similar framework.

2025: S5304

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shalt take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become law, provided however, that if chapter 696 of the laws of 2025
have not taken affect on or before such date then section five of this
act shalt take effect on the same date and in the same manner as such
chapter of the laws of 2025 take effect.

summary: Enacts the "New York travel insurance act" regulating the licensing and registration of limited lines travel insurance producers and travel retailers, and the sale and marketing of travel insurance and related products.
